Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
As per office report, the opposite party no.2 has refused to accept the notice.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State of U.P. and perused the record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellants with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 28.11.2022 passed by learned Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Deoria in Bail Application No.
2615 of 2022, arising out of Case Crime No. 113 of 2022, under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC, Section 67 of I.T. (Amendment) Act, and Section 3(2)5 of SC/ST Act, Police Station Bariyarpur, District Deoria.

sentences.text: At the time of filling of the examination form, the appellant had taken the mobile number of the victim and continued to talk with her.

On 5.6.2022 when the victim went to market, the appellant met her and offered to take cold drink, she refused,
on refusal, he got annoyed, the victim consumed the cold drink and became unconscious.
The appellant took her on his motorcycle to some unknown place and committed rape with her, clicked obscene video and photographs.
On the next day, on the pretext to make the viral obscene video, the appellant tried to establish physical relations with the victim and the appellant also used caste related words.
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that the appellant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The appellant has not made viral any video of the prosecutrix.
As per DCRB report the maternal uncle of the victim did not want to allow the victim to meet with appellant.
It is further submitted that the victim is major and she understands the consequences of rape.
During her medical examination, no sign of rape has been observed by the doctor concerned.
Lastly, it is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that there is no chance of the appellant fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The appellant is languishing in jail since 22.11.2022 and in case he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the early disposal of the case.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the victim in her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. as well in the FIR has consistently stated that inspite of protest the appellant established physical relations, took her mobile number and used to make calls.
The appellant is a married person having one daughter.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the act of the appellant played in the commission of crime, who is a married person having one child, I do not find it fit case for bail.

Since the trial court has passed the impugned order after appreciating the evidence available on record, there is no occasion to interfere with the finding of fact recorded by the trial court, hence,
the present criminal appeal lacks merit and deserves to be dismissed.
Accordingly, the criminal appeal is dismissed.

However, the trial court is directed to expedite the trial and make every endeavour to conclude the same expeditiously, preferably, within a period of one year from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties subject to full co-operation by the appellant, if there is no legal impediment.
Order Date :- 20.7.2023 Prajapati  Dharmendra Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84886089/
